# 4 Maccabees Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Seven Brothers Before Antiochus

---

**1** When the tyrant's eloquence had been refuted by the noble-minded speech of Eleazar, the guards brought seven brothers, handsome and modest and well-born and altogether charming, along with their aged mother.

**2** When Antiochus saw them grouped around their mother, he was pleased with them and said:

**3** Young men, I look on each of you with favor and I wish to extend my friendship to you. I give you my solemn assurance that if you transgress your ancestral tradition and conform to Greek customs, I will make you princes and appoint you to positions of honor in my service.

**4** But if you defy me by your stubbornness, you will compel me to destroy every last one of you with terrible tortures.

**5** Have pity on yourselves. Even I, your enemy, have compassion on your youth and your beauty.

**6** Will you not reflect and reconsider, and turn away from the foolishness of your ancestral customs?

**7** When Antiochus had spoken these words, the eldest of the brothers replied on behalf of all of them:

**8** What is it that you wish to ask of us, and what do you intend to learn from us? For we are ready to die rather than transgress our ancestral commandments.

**9** We would be shaming our ancestors if we did not obey the law and take reason as our guide in everything.

**10** O tyrannical king! Do not suppose that you can prevail over reason in us. We regard ourselves as already dead before you even begin your tortures.

**11** We are not moved by any of your threats, for we hold the law to be more powerful than all compulsion.

**12** We will not transgress the commands of our father Moses under any circumstances whatsoever.

**13** And if, O tyrant, you torture us for our disobedience and then put us to death, remember that you only bring a short-lived suffering upon us.

**14** But you will receive from the divine justice the eternal torments of fire for your impiety.

**15** Are you not ashamed, O man of great power against the powerless, to tear apart the limbs of those who share your own nature?

**16** Even enemies spare those whom they have captured and imprisoned; but you, our most bitter foe, torture us in our own bodies.

**17** But all this confirms for us that reason is sovereign over the passions.

**18** For had we been weak and given to passion, we would yield to you and be led astray. But we have been trained in wisdom and strengthened in devotion by the law.

**19** You must know, O Antiochus, that the laws given by Moses to our fathers are our strength, and we will never transgress them.

**20** And now, if it pleases you to torture us for refusing, proceed!
